summary: The prepared_gaia version is a Python CrewAI-style design-and-code implementation that defines many specialized agents and task descriptions for departments, opinion platforms, price platforms, and reporting. It is more explicit about agent roles and reporter context than the other versions, but it has no real tools or data-source integrations and falls back to a mock result on execution errors.

findings.description: The customer/address role is represented, but there is no implemented address lookup or property data retrieval tool.
findings.evidence: agents/customer_agent.py:10 says the customer provides the address; the file list contains agents, main.py, tasks.py, README.md, and requirements.txt, but no tools package.

findings.description: Planned investment coverage is modeled through multiple department agents, but it remains task text without implemented government-source access.
findings.evidence: agents/department_agent.py:10-15 targets planned investments and official government sources; main.py:55-58 creates district, voivodeship, city, and county tasks.

findings.description: Opinion coverage is modeled across named platforms, but there are no platform connectors or tools.
findings.evidence: agents/opinion_agent.py:10-15 describes local service reviews; main.py:61-64 creates Google, Booking, Facebook, and Tripadvisor tasks.

findings.description: Price comparison is modeled across named listing platforms, but no listing-source integration is present.
findings.evidence: agents/price_agent.py:10-15 describes comparing property prices; main.py:67-69 creates OLX, Otodom, and Allegro price tasks.

findings.description: The reporter task explicitly receives all specialist task outputs as context.
findings.evidence: tasks.py:75-90 defines reporter_task with context=list(context_tasks); main.py:72 passes department, opinion, and price tasks into reporter_task.

findings.description: Communication is defined as sequential CrewAI tasks with reporter context, but message formats, validation, and error paths are not specified.
findings.evidence: main.py:75-106 creates a Crew with process=Process.sequential; tasks.py defines descriptions and expected_output but no typed schemas or fallback contracts.

findings.description: Execution errors are converted into a demonstration mock result, which can hide real failures.
findings.evidence: main.py:121-125 prints the exception, announces a mock result, and returns "Mock result for demonstration purposes".

findings.description: The main function is large and contains TODO markers for incomplete implementation areas.
findings.evidence: main.py:19 defines a main function measured at 109 lines; TODO/FIXME markers were found at lines 42, 68, 72, 88, and 102.

findings.description: The implementation relies on print statements for execution flow and error reporting.

missing_requirements: Implemented property search by address against a real or structured property source.
Implemented retrieval from official government sources.
Implemented retrieval from real estate offer platforms.
A report produced from actual collected data rather than task descriptions or a mock fallback.
logical_inconsistencies: README.md:3 calls the system production-grade, but main.py:121-125 returns a mock result when execution fails.
The architecture defines many source-specific agents, but no tools or connectors exist for those sources.
implementation_risks: The system may appear to complete analysis even when core execution fails because exceptions lead to a mock demonstration result.
Without tools or connectors, agents can only rely on LLM-generated text rather than verifiable government, review, or listing data.
TODO markers in main.py indicate incomplete setup for multiple platform-specific agents.
